verbs.summary: retire a dead ~/work repo: git-bundle all history into ~/work/archive/<year>/, mark hub archived
verbs.hints: Retire a dead ~/work repo to a restorable git bundle. Common mistake: run it on the repo you're still using — it removes the working tree (bundle restores it).

verbs.summary: commit/push nag (bare); restic family + git-bundle net: init|status|run|drill|bundle
verbs.usage: ops backup [status | run [--target local|cloud] --yes | drill --yes | bundle [--dry-run] | init --yes]
verbs.hints: Bare `ops backup` is the UNCHANGED read-only commit/push nag (exit 1 = at risk; never pushes for you). Subcommands add the restic durability floor (auto-detected; degrades with an install hint): init (human-run once, --yes, writes .backup/config.json with op:// REFERENCES + renders the launchd plist), status (snapshot age per target, exit 1 if stale >48h or unconfigured), run [--target local|cloud] (cloud is --yes ALWAYS; the scheduled cloud push runs from launchd DIRECTLY with an append-only B2 key, outside this verb), drill (--yes; restore latest snapshot to tmp and diff), bundle (git bundle --all of ~/ops + every ~/work repo into ~/files/backups/bundles/ with retention). Common mistake: expecting bare backup to run restic — it only nags; use `ops backup run`.

verbs.summary: save a URL as a wiki note (type: bookmark); best-effort title fetch; --archive snapshots to ~/files
verbs.hints: Save a URL as a wiki bookmark note (title fetched best-effort). Body text is extracted via trafilatura when installed (optional dep; pip install trafilatura), else a crude zero-dependency tag-strip. --archive additionally snapshots the fetched page HTML into ~/files/bookmarks/ against link-rot (skipped if the page wasn't reachable). Any http(s) URL is accepted as a generic link/article — a tweet or video URL is saved the same way, there is no special x.com/YouTube parsing (see `ops files extract` for transcript extraction of an already-ingested media file). Common mistake: --archive without a reachable page — the HTML snapshot is skipped.

verbs.summary: thought -> inbox (also: pipe stdin)
verbs.hints: Zero-decision dump of a thought into inbox/ for later triage. Common mistake: using it for an actionable to-do — use `ops task add` instead.

verbs.summary: daily close: summarize the day into the journal, flag loose ends
verbs.hints: Daily close: writes a facts digest (commits, completed, stalled) into the journal. Common mistake: expecting prose — the shell fallback logs facts only.

verbs.summary: nightly dream-lite pass: wiki orphans/stale + day digest into the journal
verbs.hints: Nightly zero-LLM maintenance: wiki orphans/stale + day digest into the journal. Common mistake: scheduling something heavier — this is read + one journal append.

verbs.summary: self-check: tools, folders, manifest, adapters, secrets, index (--init creates folders)
verbs.hints: Self-check: tools, folders, manifest, secrets, sync-wall. --init creates missing folders. Common mistake: ignoring a FAIL (exit 1) — WARN is advisory, FAIL is not.

verbs.summary: generate {description, keywords} for a note's derived text, written to its frontmatter
verbs.hints: Generate a description + keywords for one note (source: its .extract.md if it has one, else its own body) and write them to the note's frontmatter — never to the .extract.md, which --reextract rewrites. Idempotent via an enrich_key: hash of (model, text); a plain re-run on unchanged text is a no-op, --reenrich forces. --all sweeps every note lacking a current key, sequentially, under one warm model load. Auto-wired (best-effort) into `files extract` and `bookmark` unless OPS_ENRICH=off. Common mistake: expecting meta on the .extract.md — it lives on the shadow/primary note.

verbs.summary: binary assets: ingest [<path>] [--client|--project|--area <slug>|--research] [--extract] | extract <slug> | distill <slug> | link <file> <hub> | list | open <slug>
verbs.usage: ops files ingest [<path>] [--client|--project|--area <slug> | --research] [--extract] | extract <slug> [--reextract] [--heavy] [--lang <x>] [--diarize] [--describe] | distill <slug> | link <file> <hub> | list [--hub <slug>] | open <slug>
verbs.hints: The binary-assets plane: ingest routes a file into ~/files + writes a wiki shadow note; extract emits a SIBLING derived note wiki/files/<slug>.extract.md (type extract|transcript, derived_from/source_sha256/tool) from the source bytes via an auto-detected media tier: pdf -> markdown, audio/video/URL -> transcript, image -> OCR/VLM description, txt/md -> plain text. Each tier is an optional dep (pymupdf4llm/docling, mlx-whisper/faster-whisper/parakeet-mlx, yt-dlp, ocrmac/tesseract) that degrades to a one-line install hint instead of crashing; a URL source needs a shadow note whose path: is already the URL (no ingest <url> support yet). distill compiles that extract into 1-N author:agent/status:draft concept notes in wiki/notes/ (typed JSON payload with an agent, heading-outline fallback without; promote via `ops triage drafts`). Same-bytes+same-tool re-run is a no-op; --reextract forces. Common mistake: expecting the binary in git — only the plaintext shadow + extract notes are tracked; and expecting a transcript without the tier's dep installed (it degrades with an install hint).

verbs.summary: list verbs / usage for one (rendered from ops.json)
verbs.hints: The surface itself: verbs, capabilities, per-verb I/O contract. Read this first; never invent a verb. Common mistake: hardcoding a verb list instead of reading ops.json.

verbs.summary: rebuild the search index over wiki (FTS5 + graph; +LanceDB if OPS_VECTORS=1); --changed = mtime fast path; --manifest regenerates ops.json
verbs.hints: Rebuild the FTS5 + graph search index over wiki (+vectors if OPS_VECTORS). `--changed` is the fast path after external Obsidian edits (reindex only files touched since the last build). Common mistake: searching before indexing — an empty index returns no hits.

verbs.summary: DRAFT an invoice for a client (reads tax-formula.md; computes VAT; never sends)
verbs.hints: DRAFT an invoice (computes VAT); never sends. Common mistake: expecting delivery — you export and send by hand.

verbs.summary: list | run <name> | apply — scheduler-neutral jobs (§15); apply renders launchd plists
verbs.hints: Scheduler-neutral jobs: list/run/apply. Only read/safe_write may be scheduled. Common mistake: a job with inline shell logic — a job calls exactly ONE verb.

verbs.summary: download/offload/test surface for the model layer: list|status|stop|pull|test per stage (stt, ocr, vlm, enrich, embed, rerank)
verbs.usage: ops models list | status | stop [--all] [<model>] | pull [--stage <s>|--all] --yes | test <stage> [--model <m>] [--input <file>] --yes
reads: OPS_OCR / OPS_VLM / OPS_ENRICH_MODEL / OPS_EMBED_MODEL / OPS_RERANK_MODEL env
writes: ollama's local model store (pull only; outside ~/ops)
verbs.hints: Per-stage model management, env-config-driven (proposal docs/design/proposals/2026-07-07-search-enrichment-pipeline.md §2.1). `list` shows each stage's configured model, runtime, and whether it's pulled/available — pure probes, never loads a model. `status` is `ollama ps` (resident models). `stop [--all]` unloads a resident model (`ollama stop`) — free of --yes, it just reloads on next use. `pull [--stage <s>|--all]` and `test <stage> [--model <m>] [--input <file>]` both self-gate: without --yes they refuse with EXIT_CONFIRM(3) and print the exact re-run, because both can pull gigabytes; test then runs the stage's configured (or --model override) model on a sample/--input and prints output + timing, so you can A/B a candidate before adopting it by setting its env var. stt/rerank are pip-managed runtimes, not ollama models — pull skips them with a note. Common mistake: expecting `pull`/`test` to run without --yes — they never do, by design.

verbs.summary: scaffold a project (wiki hub + ~/work repo), client (wiki hub + ~/files tree), or verb (bin/<name>/ stub)
verbs.usage: ops new project "<name>" [--kind labs|products|tools] | new client "<name>" | new verb <name> [--risk <class>] [--summary "<text>"]
verbs.hints: Scaffold a project (wiki hub + ~/work repo), client (hub + ~/files tree), or verb. Common mistake: a slug that collides — slugs are globally unique across the three roots.

verbs.summary: resolve & open anything: task id | wiki slug | files asset | search top hit
verbs.hints: One resolver for every addressable thing (task id → wiki slug → files shadow → search top hit). Default PRINTS the path — never launches a GUI. --edit ($EDITOR), --reveal (Finder open -R), --obsidian (obsidian:// URI via wiki open). Bare `ops open` with fzf = fuzzy picker with preview.

verbs.summary: self-organization loop: scan -> review -> apply typed ops (proposal queue, never direct edits)
verbs.usage: ops organize scan [--dry-run] | review [--accept|--reject|--defer <ids|all>] [--dry-run|--yes] | apply [--yes|--dry-run] [--safe-only] [--max-ops N] [--max-lines N]
writes: wiki/ (apply only, one git commit per op)
verbs.hints: The self-organization loop. scan does ZERO-LLM candidate generation into a typed proposal queue inbox/organize/<date>.jsonl (CLOSED op catalog: add_link, refresh_hub, normalize_tag, fix_frontmatter, retitle, flag_duplicate, propose_merge; validated at write AND read time). A model (OPS_AGENT) only RANKS confidences; with none, heuristics. review appends accept/reject/defer status lines (audit ledger, latest wins) and shows the exact diff each op would produce. apply (needs --yes, NEVER schedulable; apply --dry-run previews the exact replay and writes nothing) deterministically replays APPROVED ops only, one commit per op, with an edit budget (20 ops / 300 lines, flags may only lower it) and protected paths (conventions/index/hubs/pinned) review-only; retitle/propose_merge/deletions never auto-apply. --safe-only applies only the four additive primitives above 0.8. Common mistake: expecting apply to run a model (it never does) or to touch a protected path.

verbs.summary: one-call session bootstrap: journal tail, tasks, inbox, proposals, index/backup age, git, recent notes
verbs.hints: Read-only session bootstrap for humans and agents in one call. --json = the full envelope; --line = a ≤60-char string cached (short TTL, OPS_ORIENT_TTL) for a starship/tmux prompt hook. Common mistake: confusing it with `ops start`, which writes the journal.

verbs.summary: install/list/trust/update/remove plugin packs (untrusted until you trust them)
verbs.usage: ops plugin add <owner/repo|path>[@tag] --yes | list | trust <name> --yes | update <name> --yes | remove <name> --yes
verbs.hints: Installs a pack under plugins/<name>/, but its verbs are capped at confirm until `ops plugin trust <name> --yes` — self-declared risk never takes effect at install. add/update/remove/trust need --yes; list is read-only. Common mistake: expecting a freshly added pack to run at its declared risk.

verbs.summary: ~/work fleet: health | clone <slug>|--all | adopt <path> --kind <k> | nuke-modules --stale <days>
verbs.hints: The ~/work fleet manager: health/clone/adopt/nuke-modules. health exit 1 = repos need attention. Common mistake: adopting into the wrong --kind (products|labs|tools).

verbs.summary: ranked file#heading hits (keyword + graph [+ vectors/rerank])
verbs.hints: Ranked file#heading hits with an FTS5 snippet excerpt (keyword + graph, +vectors if OPS_VECTORS). `--author human` excludes agent + derived material; `--author agent` keeps only agent notes (provenance planes). `--open` jumps to the top hit via `ops open`; bare `ops search` in a tty with fzf opens a live search session. Common mistake: running before `ops index`, or too narrow a query — broaden and reindex.

verbs.summary: zero-knowledge share: render+encrypt a note (or tag collection) locally, publish only ciphertext
verbs.usage: ops share <slug> [--expires 7d] [--plain|--gist] [--dry-run|--yes] | collection <tag> | list | revoke <id> --yes | init
verbs.hints: Share a note or `collection <tag>` as ONE self-contained HTML blob, encrypted AES-256-GCM LOCALLY; only CIPHERTEXT is published to a Cloudflare Worker+KV and the key rides the URL `#fragment` (the provider can never read it). Transmitting subactions (share/collection/revoke) self-gate --yes -> EXIT_CONFIRM(3); `list` is free. `--dry-run` renders+encrypts locally and stops. `--plain` = unguessable slug, no E2E. `--gist` = secret gist fallback. Run `ops share init` once to deploy the worker. Common mistake: expecting it to send the link — output is a DRAFT link, the human sends it.

verbs.summary: daily start: today's journal, carry-forward open tasks, dashboard
verbs.hints: Daily start: opens today's journal, carries forward open tasks, shows the dashboard. Common mistake: expecting it to be read-only — it seeds and logs to the journal.

verbs.summary: dashboard: active/waiting tasks, inbox, last index, repo state
verbs.hints: One-screen dashboard: tasks, inbox, index freshness, git state. Read-class. Common mistake: confusing it with `ops start` (which writes the journal).

verbs.summary: decay Desktop/Downloads: untouched 7d → _swept/YYYY-MM/, 60d in _swept → Trash
verbs.hints: Decay Desktop/Downloads: untouched 7d → _swept/, 60d in _swept → Trash (never deletes outright). Common mistake: expecting rescue by reopening — rescue is `ops files ingest`.

verbs.summary: list | add "<title>" | show <id> | move <id> <status> | done <id>
verbs.hints: The task system: list/add/show/move/done. Common mistake: inventing a status — it must be one of inbox/active/waiting/done.

verbs.summary: propose filing of inbox/ items into tasks or wiki; human approves | drafts: promote agent-drafted notes
verbs.hints: Propose filing of inbox/ items into a task or note; the human approves. `ops triage drafts` pages agent-drafted notes (author:agent, status:draft) from `ops files distill` as a promotion queue: accept -> active, reject -> delete, one git commit each. --json lists proposals/drafts without acting. Common mistake: expecting it to auto-file without --yes.

verbs.summary: weekly review: shipped/stalled, repo health, sweep done/ -> done/<year>/
verbs.hints: Weekly review: shipped vs stalled, repo health, sweeps done/ into done/<year>/. Common mistake: running it mid-week expecting it not to sweep — it always sweeps completed tasks.

verbs.summary: open <slug> [--obsidian] | edit | new <type> <name> | backlinks | stale | orphans | canvas <hub|#tag> | list
verbs.hints: Navigate/grow the wiki: open/edit/new/backlinks/stale/orphans/canvas/list. `open --obsidian` (or OPS_OPEN=obsidian) opens the note in Obsidian via a local obsidian:// URI. `canvas <hub|#tag>` writes a deterministic wiki/canvas/<slug>.canvas (JSON Canvas). Common mistake: a duplicate slug on `new` — slugs are unique.
